Numbered paragraphs follow in the main column; no margin notes. Below the text, the word "Exer-" stands alone at the right as a catchword.

main_text.p: Ad probationem ex definitione Ramæa, per negationem: quia definitio est vitiosa: Probetur
1. quia argumentum est definiendum actu non potentia.
2. alioqui sex & pluribus argumentis sæpe cōstabit syllogismus, quoniam tot sæpe vocabulis syllogismus constat.
3. Authoritate Ciceronis, Quintiliani & omnium recte loquentium.
4. Ramo opponatur Ramus in prioribus omnibus dialecticis: ubi recte definivit argumentum esse quod aliquid arguit.
Ad III. per concessionem in natura, & arte operante, æmula naturæ: non autem in arte docente, quæ ab idea necessario incipit.
Ad IV. Resp. 1. Cicero sequitur Stoicorum partitionem, cujus incommoda supra sunt ostensa.
11. Opponitur authoritas Aristotelis, cui ut maiori artifici in sua arte magis credendum est.
Conclusio: sit hortatio, ut de his sedulo cogitet, & veterem Logicam prius recte intelligere, quā cum novatoribus fastidire discat.

page.notes: The brace after items 1–3 is a bracket joining them to "tradere"; it is transcribed inline above. Item "I I." in the paragraph before "Conclusio" is read as "11." and may be a printing variant. The word "syllogismus" in item 2 and "syllogismo" in item 3 may be misprints for "syllogismus" as printed; the scan reads "fyllogismo" and "fyllogismus" with long-s forms, transcribed as plain s. Abbreviation "cūm" in the last line is read as "cum". The bottom of the page shows a faint printer's mark, not transcribed. "Exer-" is a catchword at the right of the last line.
